[codex] ## Operating Context
[codex] 
[codex] This repository coordinates the deployment and development environment for the Budget Analyzer application, a reference microservices architecture used as an open source learning resource for AI-assisted development.
[codex] 
[codex] This project is designed for AI-assisted development. The containerized development environment lives in the sibling `../workspace` repository; that repo owns the devcontainer configuration.
[codex] 
[codex] The `ext-authz` Go service implementation lives in the sibling `../ext-authz`
[codex] repository. This orchestration repository owns its Kubernetes manifests, Istio
[codex] `ext_authz` wiring, NGINX integration, Redis ACL wiring, production image
[codex] policy, and deployment documentation.
[codex] 
[codex] The default debugging model is split across host and container:
[codex] - Tilt runs on the host machine
[codex] - AI agents run inside the container
[codex] - The container has shared workspace access and full `kubectl` access to the host-managed cluster
[codex] 
[codex] The agent container is inside the trusted local-development boundary. Local
[codex] workspace files, the local Kind kubeconfig and Kubernetes Secrets, generated
[codex] development TLS keys, and disposable local API-test credentials are not hidden
[codex] from the agent. Never expose staging or production kubeconfigs, cloud or
[codex] deployment credentials, user credentials, or session cookies to this
[codex] container, and never use an agent session to deploy or administer staging or
[codex] production. Before an in-container agent-authorized cluster mutation, require
[codex] the current context and referenced cluster to equal `kind-kind`, require a
[codex] loopback Kubernetes API endpoint, and require the `kind-control-plane` node.
[codex] Use `kind get clusters` only as an additional host-side check because the
[codex] container Docker daemon cannot enumerate the host-managed Kind cluster. For
[codex] the full boundary and API-test target checks, read
[codex] `docs/architecture/autonomous-ai-execution.md` before changing agent sandbox,
[codex] credential, Kubernetes-access, or autonomous execution behavior.
[codex] 
[codex] Production target is Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Free Tier on ARM64:
[codex] - Shape: `VM.Standard.A1.Flex`
[codex] - Capacity: 4 OCPUs, 24 GB RAM
[codex] - OS baseline: Ubuntu 22.04 Minimal
[codex] - Region baseline: Phoenix
[codex] - Deployment model: single-node, production-grade demo environment
[codex] 
[codex] Architecture implications:
[codex] - All container images must support `linux/arm64`
[codex] - Local Tilt/Kind and OCI/k3s are both treated as production-grade deployment paths
[codex] - Observability remains internal-only in both environments
[codex] 
[codex] Architecture principles:
[codex] - Production parity between local Tilt/Kind and OCI/k3s
[codex] - Microservices with clear service boundaries and independent deployability
[codex] - Session-based edge authorization for browser security and session management
[codex] - Istio ingress handles ext_authz and auth-path throttling; NGINX handles API routing, backend/API rate limiting, and load balancing
[codex] - Resource-based routing keeps the frontend decoupled from service topology
[codex] - Defense in depth across Istio ingress, Session Gateway or NGINX, and downstream services
[codex] - Kubernetes-native development uses Tilt live update so code changes reach running pods quickly while the full security stack stays active; see `docs/development/local-environment.md#live-development-pipeline`
[codex] 
[codex] Technology pattern:
[codex] - Frontend: React web application
[codex] - Backends: Spring Boot + Java + Gradle
[codex] - Browser auth edge: Session Gateway (Spring WebFlux)
[codex] - External authorization: `ext-authz` Go service
[codex] - Edge and routing: Istio ingress/egress plus NGINX API gateway
[codex] - Infrastructure: PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ
[codex] - Monitoring: Prometheus, Grafana, Jaeger, Kiali
[codex] 
[codex] Service topology summary:
[codex] - Frontend: React web application for browser clients
[codex] - Backend workloads: Spring Boot microservices behind NGINX, plus Session Gateway and `ext-authz` on the auth and authorization path
[codex] - Infrastructure: PostgreSQL, Redis, and RabbitMQ in the `infrastructure` namespace; Redis `/data` is PVC-backed through the `redis-data` claim template
[codex] - Monitoring: Prometheus, Grafana, kube-state-metrics, the repo-managed Jaeger v2 backend, and standalone Kiali in `monitoring`; Jaeger and Kiali stay `ClusterIP`-only
[codex] - Ingress and egress: Istio ingress handles browser entry, `ext_authz`, and auth-path throttling; Istio egress stays `ClusterIP` with `REGISTRY_ONLY`
[codex] - Exact service ports and exposure rules live in `docs/architecture/port-reference.md`
[codex] 
[codex] Adding a new service:
[codex] - Create manifests in `kubernetes/services/{name}/`
[codex] - Register the service in `Tiltfile`
[codex] - Add NGINX routes when the service owns public resources
[codex] - See `docs/architecture/session-edge-authorization-pattern.md` and `nginx/README.md`
[codex] 
[codex] Version numbers and concrete dependency selections live in service repos, manifests, and checked-in release inputs, not in this file.
[codex]

[codex] ## Core Runtime Pattern
[codex] 
[codex] The primary request flow is:
[codex] 
[codex] ```text
[codex] Browser -> Istio Ingress -> ext_authz validates session -> NGINX -> services
[codex] Auth paths -> Istio Ingress -> Session Gateway
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] Entry-point ownership:
[codex] - Browser auth lifecycle stays on the direct Session Gateway lane
[codex] - API traffic stays on the NGINX lane with ingress-layer `ext_authz`
[codex] - Exact route ownership and `/api-docs` behavior live in `docs/architecture/session-edge-authorization-pattern.md` and `docs-aggregator/README.md`
[codex] 
[codex] Session and identity rules:
[codex] - Session Gateway resolves roles and permissions from `permission-service` during session creation and owns browser session lifecycle on the direct auth lane
[codex] - Keep browser session logic on the direct `/auth/*` lane rather than pushing it through the general API path
[codex] - Exact browser endpoints and the shared Session Gateway/`ext_authz` contract live in `docs/architecture/session-edge-authorization-pattern.md`
[codex] 
[codex] Operational guardrails:
[codex] - Follow the resource-based routing pattern for new API endpoints
[codex] - Treat any new public `/api/...` route as incomplete until both `nginx/nginx.k8s.conf` and `nginx/nginx.production.k8s.conf` claim it and verification proves it does not fall through to the SPA
[codex] - Keep Spring Boot workloads on the startup/readiness/liveness probe pattern used by the checked-in manifests
[codex] - Keep PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, and Redis on their repo-owned stateful deployment patterns
[codex] - Redis `/data` is PVC-backed. Do not treat pod replacement or `tilt down` as a Redis reset. Use `./scripts/ops/flush-redis.sh` for a logical reset, or recreate the cluster/runtime when a full clean state is required
[codex] 
[codex] Observability rules:
[codex] - Grafana, Prometheus, Jaeger, and Kiali are internal-only in both local Tilt and OCI/k3s
[codex] - Use loopback-only access for operators: raw `kubectl port-forward --address 127.0.0.1 ...` or `./scripts/ops/start-observability-port-forwards.sh`
[codex] - `./scripts/smoketest/verify-observability-port-forward-access.sh` is the focused access proof
[codex] - Do not introduce public observability hostnames
[codex] - Do not use `--address 0.0.0.0` for observability access
[codex] - Exact observability access commands, local ports, and Kiali auth flow live in `docs/architecture/observability.md`
[codex]

[codex] 
[codex] ## Image Pinning And Supply Chain Guardrails
[codex] 
[codex] - Treat checked-in third-party image refs and Dockerfile base images as digest-pinning targets unless an exception is explicitly documented in the executable inventories
[codex] - The executable inventories live in `scripts/lib/image-pinning-targets.txt` and `scripts/lib/allowed-latest-image-refs.txt`
[codex] - Keep those inventories aligned with the static security guardrail checks
[codex] - Only the documented local image repos may remain on `:latest` in checked-in manifests
[codex] - Live Tilt deploys rewrite those same repos to immutable `:tilt-&lt;hash>` refs and currently force `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` on those managed deploys
[codex] - Treat every third-party `image:` or `FROM` ref as a digest-pinning target unless it is explicitly excluded in the inventories
[codex] - `tests/setup-flow` and `tests/security-preflight` are stale, non-gating retained assets until they are explicitly realigned to the current Istio-only baseline. Do not treat them as current completion gates
[codex] 
[codex] ## Cross-Repo Boundaries
[codex] 
[codex] Do NOT write code in sibling repositories from this repo context.
[codex] 
[codex] Allowed write surface from this repo:
[codex] - This repository
[codex] - Documentation in sibling repos
[codex] - Configuration in sibling repos when fixing deployment, environment, or manifest wiring issues
[codex] 
[codex] If a fix requires service logic changes in a sibling repo:
[codex] - Stop
[codex] - Describe the needed service-side change clearly
[codex] - Let the user handle it, or switch to that repo's context
[codex] 
[codex] Do not hide sibling-repo contract failures with orchestration workarounds.
[codex] 
[codex] Example: if Spring Boot services fail to expose `/actuator/prometheus` and that contract belongs in `service-common`, fix or rebuild `service-common`. Do not patch orchestration manifests with compensating `MANAGEMENT_ENDPOINTS_WEB_EXPOSURE_INCLUDE=health,prometheus` overrides just to hide the defect.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Production-Grade Parity
[codex] 
[codex] Treat both supported runtime paths, local Tilt/Kind and OCI/k3s, as production-grade microservices deployments.
[codex] 
[codex] Do not present the following as durable fixes:
[codex] - manual live-cluster drift
[codex] - security bypasses
[codex] - relaxed policies
[codex] - untracked Helm overrides
[codex] - degraded persistence such as replacing StatefulSets with `emptyDir`
[codex] - orchestration-level compensations for service-owned defects
[codex] 
[codex] Temporary recovery commands are acceptable only when clearly labeled as diagnostics or incident-recovery steps. Every durable fix must be repo-owned, repeatable from scripts/manifests, documented in the affected runbook or plan, and verified with the relevant smoke or guardrail checks.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Planning Transparency
[codex] 
[codex] Write plans to `docs/plans/`, not hidden locations.
[codex] 
[codex] Plans should be visible, version-controlled collaboration artifacts. Do not hide meaningful project planning in ephemeral or private planning mechanisms.
[codex] 
[codex] When creating an implementation or execution plan intended for AI Session
[codex] Handler, follow the [AI Session Handler plan format](../ai-session-handler/docs/plan-format.md), use
[codex] its canonical template, replace every placeholder, and retain the numbered `## Phase N: Title`
[codex] headings.
[codex] 
[codex] Run a specific plan through the workspace wrapper with:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] ai-session-handler run \
[codex]   --plan /workspace/REPOSITORY/docs/plans/PLAN.md \
[codex]   --max-phases 999 \
[codex]   --quiet \
[codex]   --agent-cmd "/workspace/ai-session-handler/.venv/bin/ai-session-handler-codex-high --model MODEL"
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] Omit `--model MODEL` from the quoted agent command to use the wrapper's
[codex] configured or default model.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Autonomous AI Execution Pattern
[codex] 
[codex] The preferred AI execution pattern in this repo is autonomous execution with clear success criteria. For rationale, safety model, Docker access patterns, and examples, see `docs/architecture/autonomous-ai-execution.md`.
[codex] 
[codex] ## SSL/TLS Certificate Constraints
[codex] 
[codex] NEVER run SSL write operations from the AI container.
[codex] 
[codex] The container has its own `mkcert` CA, but the user's browser trusts the host CA. Certificates generated inside the container will cause browser trust failures.
[codex] 
[codex] Forbidden operations that must be run by the user on the host:
[codex] - `mkcert`
[codex] - `openssl genrsa`
[codex] - `openssl req -new`
[codex] - `openssl x509 -req`
[codex] - Any script that generates browser or infrastructure certificates, including `scripts/bootstrap/setup-k8s-tls.sh` and `scripts/bootstrap/setup-infra-tls.sh`
[codex] 
[codex] Allowed read-only operations:
[codex] - `openssl x509 -text -noout`
[codex] - `openssl verify`
[codex] - `kubectl get secret -o yaml`
[codex] - Certificate file reads for debugging
[codex] 
[codex] For live agent work against exactly
[codex] `https://app.budgetanalyzer.localhost`, agents may run the workspace-owned
[codex] `ensure-budget-analyzer-local-ca-trust` command to install the host-published
[codex] public root into container-local trust stores. Use
[codex] `check-budget-analyzer-local-ca-trust` for read-only trust diagnosis. Read
[codex] `../workspace/docs/local-budget-analyzer-tls.md` before changing or debugging
[codex] this flow.
[codex] 
[codex] If `nginx/certs/k8s/_mkcert-rootCA.pem` is missing, invalid, or stale, stop and
[codex] ask the user to run `./setup.sh` from the orchestration checkout on the host.
[codex] Do not generate or rotate certificates in-container, and do not bypass
[codex] verification with HTTP, `--insecure`, `verify=False`, or
[codex] `ignore_https_errors`.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Path Portability
[codex] 
[codex] Never hardcode absolute workspace paths such as `/workspace`.
[codex] 
[codex] Use relative paths or dynamically resolved paths instead:
[codex] - `../service-common`
[codex] - `$(dirname "$0")`
[codex] - Tilt variables such as `config.main_dir`
[codex] 
[codex] All repositories are expected to be cloned side-by-side under a common parent directory so cross-repo relative references continue to work.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Historical Docs
[codex] 
[codex] Ignore `docs/archive/` for active implementation work.
[codex] 
[codex] Use `docs/decisions/` for context and rationale, not as an implementation surface. Do not edit decision records unless explicitly asked.
[codex] 
[codex] ## NO GIT WRITE OPERATIONS
[codex] 
[codex] Never run git write commands such as `commit`, `push`, `checkout`, `reset`, or branch manipulation without explicit user request. The user owns git workflow entirely.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Honest Discourse
[codex] 
[codex] Do not over-validate ideas. The user wants honest pushback, not agreement.
[codex] 
[codex] - If something seems wrong, say so directly
[codex] - Distinguish novel ideas from ideas that are obvious in retrospect
[codex] - Push back on vague claims and ask for concrete constraints
[codex] - Skip empty praise and filler
[codex] # Documentation Ownership
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Active
[codex] **Purpose:** Define the canonical owner for recurring documentation topics so
[codex] exact operational detail lives in one place and non-owner docs summarize and
[codex] link instead of copying.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Rules
[codex] 
[codex] - One recurring topic should have one canonical owner.
[codex] - Non-owner docs may give a short summary, orientation paragraph, or diagram,
[codex]   but they should not own the full command sequence, table, or contract.
[codex] - When a topic changes, update the owner doc first, then update summaries,
[codex]   indexes, and cross-links that point to it.
[codex] - `docs/archive/` is historical reference only and does not own active
[codex]   implementation detail.
[codex] - If no existing owner fits a new recurring topic, choose one and update this
[codex]   file in the same change.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Exact Detail vs. Summary
[codex] 
[codex] In this repo, "exact detail" includes things such as:
[codex] 
[codex] - full startup and verifier sequences
[codex] - complete port tables
[codex] - observability access commands
[codex] - detailed route ownership lists
[codex] - detailed `/api-docs` behavior and output definitions
[codex] 
[codex] Those details should live in the owner doc. Non-owner docs can summarize the
[codex] shape of the topic and link outward.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Ownership Map
[codex] 
[codex] | Topic | Canonical owner | Rule for non-owner docs |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- |
[codex] | Documentation ownership policy | [docs/OWNERSHIP.md](OWNERSHIP.md) | Link here instead of restating the full ownership map. |

[codex] # Dependency Update Review Baseline
[codex] 
[codex] **Date:** 2026-09-06  
[codex] **Status:** Point-in-time research  
[codex] **Purpose:** Preserve the manually researched dependency recommendations so
[codex] they can be compared with repository-owned Dependabot and Renovate findings
[codex] after that automation is enabled.
[codex] 
[codex] This is not a version contract or an implementation plan. Upstream current
[codex] versions will continue to change. Checked-in build files, manifests, version
[codex] catalogs, and `deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh` remain the sources of
[codex] truth for selected versions.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Executive Summary
[codex] 
[codex] The highest-priority work is not a blanket migration to every current major.
[codex] It is a security patch batch covering Redis, the Spring-managed dependency
[codex] stack, External Secrets Operator, Kyverno, the frontend dependency tree,
[codex] `go-redis`, the JDK runtime image, and selected observability components.
[codex] 
[codex] Several runtime lines are also unsupported or approaching end of support:
[codex] Spring Boot 3.5, Node.js 20, Go 1.24, RabbitMQ 3.13, NGINX 1.29, and production
[codex] Kubernetes/K3s 1.34. Those should be handled as explicit migration batches
[codex] rather than mixed into low-risk security patch updates.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Security And Maintenance Patch Recommendations
[codex] 
[codex] ### Redis Server
[codex] 
[codex] | Item | Finding |
[codex] | --- | --- |
[codex] | Checked-in reference | `redis:7-alpine@sha256:7aec734b...` |
[codex] | Version resolved from the digest | Redis 7.4.8, image created 2026-04-17 |
[codex] | Recommended supported-line patch | Redis 7.4.11 |
[codex] | Major migration status | Redis 8 exists, but is not required for support |
[codex] 
[codex] Redis 7.4.8 predates the May 2026 security release and is affected by multiple
[codex] authenticated memory-safety vulnerabilities, including a `RESTORE` command
[codex] issue that may lead to remote code execution. This has practical relevance to
[codex] the current ACL model: `session-gateway` and `redis-ops` receive `+@all`, while
[codex] the other service identities are substantially narrower.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: refresh the Redis 7.4 image to 7.4.11 before considering a
[codex] Redis 8 migration. Review whether `session-gateway` needs `+@all` or can use an
[codex] explicit command allowlist that excludes administrative commands such as
[codex] `RESTORE`.
[codex] 
[codex] Primary advisory:
[codex] [GHSA-c8h9-259x-jff4](https://github.com/redis/redis/security/advisories/GHSA-c8h9-259x-jff4).
[codex] 
[codex] ### Spring Boot-Managed Backend Stack
[codex] 
[codex] The checked-in Spring Boot 3.5.14 BOM resolves these notable components:
[codex] 
[codex] | Component | Boot 3.5.14 | Boot 3.5.16 | Security floor observed in this review |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- | --- |
[codex] | Spring Framework | 6.2.18 | 6.2.19 | 6.2.19 |
[codex] | Spring Security | 6.5.10 | 6.5.11 | No advisory found for 6.5.10 in the queried database |
[codex] | Jackson BOM | 2.21.2 | 2.21.4 | 2.21.4 |
[codex] | Netty | 4.1.132.Final | 4.1.135.Final | 4.1.137.Final |
[codex] | Embedded Tomcat | 10.1.54 | 10.1.55 | 10.1.58 |
[codex] 
[codex] Findings include:
[codex] 
[codex] - Spring Web 6.2.18 is affected by an `UriComponentsBuilder` SSRF advisory;
[codex]   6.2.19 contains the fix.
[codex] - Jackson 2.21.2 is affected by deserialization authorization and polymorphic
[codex]   type validation issues; the relevant 2.x fixes are present in 2.21.4.
[codex] - Netty 4.1.132 is affected by request-smuggling, decompression denial of
[codex]   service, CORS bypass, CRLF injection, and resource exhaustion advisories.
[codex] - Tomcat 10.1.54 is in the affected ranges for several authorization and
[codex]   authentication advisories. The newest reviewed fixes require 10.1.58.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: first move the coordinated Java repositories to Spring Boot
[codex] 3.5.16. Because its BOM still selects Netty 4.1.135 and Tomcat 10.1.55, assess
[codex] temporary managed-version overrides to Netty 4.1.137 and Tomcat 10.1.58. Keep
[codex] this patch batch separate from the Spring Boot 4 migration.
[codex] 
[codex] Applicability caveat: several Tomcat findings concern container-managed
[codex] FORM/DIGEST authentication, WebDAV, AJP, or direct HTTP/2 behavior that the
[codex] current services do not appear to use. The affected components are still in
[codex] the deployed classpath, so patching remains preferable to relying only on
[codex] configuration non-use. Netty is directly relevant to the reactive Session
[codex] Gateway and other WebFlux/WebClient paths.
[codex] 
[codex] Representative advisories:
[codex] 
[codex] - [Spring Framework SSRF](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7m2p-62gw-p8qq)
[codex] - [Tomcat security constraint bypass](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5m62-pw8w-7w9f)
[codex] - [Tomcat authentication bypass](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9xv2-5v5q-p794)
[codex] - [Netty request smuggling](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-38f8-5428-x5cv)
[codex] - [Netty CORS header issue](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8c42-7qj2-3j46)
[codex] - [Jackson polymorphic validation bypass](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-j3rv-43j4-c7qm)
[codex] 
[codex] ### External Secrets Operator
[codex] 
[codex] | Item | Finding |
[codex] | --- | --- |
[codex] | Checked-in chart | 2.2.0 |
[codex] | Minimum security target identified | 2.4.0 |
[codex] | Current chart at review time | 2.10.0 |
[codex] 
[codex] External Secrets 2.2.0 is affected by DNS-based secret exfiltration through
[codex] the v2 template engine and a namespace-isolation bypass in `CAProvider`
[codex] ConfigMap resolution. Because this controller handles production secrets and
[codex] has broad cluster authority, it belongs in the critical monitoring tier even
[codex] though it was omitted from the former notification guide.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: validate a direct move to the current 2.10.0 chart. Do not
[codex] remain below 2.4.0.
[codex] 
[codex] Advisories:
[codex] 
[codex] - [GHSA-r2pg-r6h7-crf3](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r2pg-r6h7-crf3)
[codex] - [GHSA-wv26-88m5-6h59](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wv26-88m5-6h59)
[codex] 
[codex] ### Kyverno
[codex] 
[codex] | Item | Finding |
[codex] | --- | --- |
[codex] | Checked-in chart/application | 3.8.0 / 1.18.0 |
[codex] | Minimum security target identified | Application 1.18.2 |
[codex] | Current chart/application at review time | 3.9.0 / 1.19.0 |
[codex] 
[codex] Kyverno 1.18.0 and 1.18.1 are affected by a critical cross-namespace resource
[codex] generation vulnerability in namespaced CEL policies. The current repository
[codex] does not define `NamespacedMutatingPolicy` or `NamespacedGeneratingPolicy`
[codex] resources, which reduces present exploitability, but the controller is a
[codex] privileged admission component.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: update the Helm chart and Kyverno CLI together to the 1.19.0
[codex] application line, then render and rerun the existing policy and security
[codex] guardrail tests.
[codex] 
[codex] Advisory:
[codex] [GHSA-79gf-7frw-68m9](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/security/advisories/GHSA-79gf-7frw-68m9).
[codex] 
[codex] ### Frontend Dependency Tree
[codex] 
[codex] `npm audit` against the checked-in lockfile reported 20 findings: 3 critical,
[codex] 13 high, 2 moderate, and 2 low. `npm audit --omit=dev` reported four high
[codex] findings associated with Axios, React Router, React Router DOM, and a
[codex] transitive Axios dependency.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommended patch batch:
[codex] 
[codex] | Package | Checked-in/locked baseline | Patch target at review time |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- |
[codex] | React / React DOM | 19.2.5 | 19.2.8 |
[codex] | React Router / React Router DOM | 7.14.2 | 7.18.3 |
[codex] | Axios | 1.16.0 | 1.20.0 |
[codex] | Vite | 6.4.2 | 6.4.3 or a separately planned major |
[codex] | Vitest packages | 3.2.4 | 3.2.7 or a separately planned major |
[codex] | PostCSS | 8.5.14 | 8.5.28 |
[codex] 
[codex] Refresh the lockfile after updating the direct dependencies so patched
[codex] versions of `form-data`, `brace-expansion`, `browserslist`, `flatted`,
[codex] `js-yaml`, `nanoid`, `picomatch`, and `ws` are selected.
[codex] 
[codex] Applicability caveats:
[codex] 
[codex] - The critical Vitest issue requires the Vitest UI server to be listening; it
[codex]   is a development-tool risk, not production browser code.
[codex] - The reviewed Vite 6.4.2 issue requires a network-exposed Windows dev server.
[codex]   The supported container path is Linux, but the patch is still low risk.
[codex] - Most React Router findings concern framework, SSR, manifest, or RSC modes.
[codex]   The application uses `BrowserRouter`, not those server modes. The open
[codex]   redirect advisory is the most relevant browser-side reason to update.

[codex]   `react-server-dom-*` package is installed. React 19.2.8 remains the sensible
[codex]   paired patch level.

[codex] when `CLIENT SETINFO` times out during connection establishment. The first
[codex] fixed version is 9.7.3; the current release at review time is 9.22.0.

[codex] `govulncheck ./...`, and the shared session-contract verifiers.

[codex] # Helper function to encode values to base64
[codex] def shell_single_quote(value):
[codex]     """Quote a string for safe single-quoted shell usage."""
[codex]     return "'" + value.replace("'", "'\"'\"'") + "'"
[codex] 
[codex] def encode_secret_data(data):
[codex]     """Encode dictionary values to base64 for Kubernetes secrets."""
[codex]     encoded = {}
[codex]     for k, v in data.items():
[codex]         encoded[k] = str(local("printf %s " + shell_single_quote(v) + " | base64 | tr -d '\\n'", quiet=True)).strip()
[codex]     return encoded
[codex] 
[codex] def json_escape(value):
[codex]     """Escape a string for safe JSON interpolation."""
[codex]     escaped = value.replace('\\', '\\\\')
[codex]     escaped = escaped.replace('"', '\\"')
[codex]     escaped = escaped.replace('\b', '\\b')
[codex]     escaped = escaped.replace('\f', '\\f')
[codex]     escaped = escaped.replace('\n', '\\n')
[codex]     escaped = escaped.replace('\r', '\\r')
[codex]     escaped = escaped.replace('\t', '\\t')
[codex]     return escaped
[codex] 
[codex] def json_string(value):
[codex]     """Render a JSON string literal."""
[codex]     return '"' + json_escape(value) + '"'
[codex]

[codex]     }
[codex]   ],

[codex]       "write": "^(amq\\\\.default|exchange-rate\\\\.import\\\\.requested|exchange-rate\\\\.import\\\\.requested\\\\.exchange-rate-import-service(\\\\.dlq)?|DLX)$",

[codex] def secret_blob(name, namespace, data):
[codex]     """Render a Kubernetes Secret as a blob."""
[codex]     encoded = encode_secret_data(data)
[codex]     lines = [
[codex]         'apiVersion: v1',
[codex]         'kind: Secret',
[codex]         'metadata:',
[codex]         '  name: ' + name,
[codex]         '  namespace: ' + namespace,
[codex]         'type: Opaque',
[codex]         'data:',
[codex]     ]
[codex]     for key in encoded:
[codex]         lines.append('  ' + key + ': ' + encoded[key])
[codex]     return blob('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
[codex] 
[codex] def create_secret(name, namespace, data):
[codex]     """Apply a Kubernetes Secret generated by Tilt."""
[codex]     k8s_yaml(secret_blob(name, namespace, data))
[codex] 
[codex] def configmap_blob(name, namespace, data):
[codex]     """Render a Kubernetes ConfigMap as a blob."""
[codex]     lines = [
[codex]         'apiVersion: v1',
[codex]         'kind: ConfigMap',
[codex]         'metadata:',
[codex]         '  name: ' + name,
[codex]         '  namespace: ' + namespace,
[codex]         'data:',
[codex]     ]
[codex]     for key, value in data.items():
[codex]         lines.append('  ' + key + ': ' + json_string(str(value)))
[codex]     return blob('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
[codex] 
[codex] def create_configmap(name, namespace, data):
[codex]     """Apply a Kubernetes ConfigMap generated by Tilt."""
[codex]     k8s_yaml(configmap_blob(name, namespace, data))

[codex] def git(repo, *args):
[codex]     result = subprocess.run(
[codex]         ["git", "-C", str(repo), *args],
[codex]         check=False,
[codex]         stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
[codex]         stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
[codex]         text=True,
[codex]     )
[codex]     if result.returncode != 0:
[codex]         return ""
[codex]     return result.stdout.strip()
[codex]

[codex] def local_source_state(artifact):
[codex]     source_repo = artifact.get("sourceRepository", "")
[codex]     repo = parent / source_repo
[codex]     manifest_ref = artifact.get("sourceRef", "")
[codex]     manifest_commit = artifact.get("sourceCommit", "")
[codex]     manifest_tag = manifest_ref.removeprefix("refs/tags/")
[codex] 
[codex]     if not repo.is_dir():
[codex]         return {
[codex]             "status": "missing-repo",
[codex]             "label": "missing repo",
[codex]             "dirty": False,
[codex]             "manifestTag": manifest_tag,
[codex]             "matchesManifestTag": False,
[codex]         }
[codex] 
[codex]     head_commit = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
[codex]     dirty = bool(git(repo, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=normal"))
[codex]     head_tags = git(repo, "tag", "--points-at", "HEAD").splitlines()
[codex]     head_tag = head_tags[0] if head_tags else ""
[codex]     manifest_tag_commit = ""
[codex] 
[codex]     if manifest_tag:
[codex]         manifest_tag_commit = git(repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"refs/tags/{manifest_tag}^{{}}")
[codex] 
[codex]     matches_manifest_tag = bool(
[codex]         head_commit
[codex]         and manifest_tag_commit
[codex]         and head_commit == manifest_tag_commit
[codex]         and (not manifest_commit or head_commit == manifest_commit)
[codex]     )
[codex] 
[codex]     if dirty and matches_manifest_tag:
[codex]         status = "modified"
[codex]         label = "modified from manifest tag"
[codex]     elif dirty:
[codex]         status = "modified"
[codex]         label = "modified local head"
[codex]     elif matches_manifest_tag:
[codex]         status = "matches-manifest-tag"
[codex]         label = "matches manifest tag"
[codex]     elif head_commit and manifest_commit and head_commit == manifest_commit:
[codex]         status = "matches-manifest-commit"
[codex]         label = "matches manifest commit"
[codex]     elif head_tag:
[codex]         status = "different-tag"
[codex]         label = f"different tag {head_tag}"
[codex]     elif head_commit:
[codex]         status = "untagged"
[codex]         label = "untagged local head"
[codex]     else:
[codex]         status = "unknown"
[codex]         label = "unknown"
[codex] 
[codex]     return {
[codex]         "status": status,
[codex]         "label": label,
[codex]         "dirty": dirty,
[codex]         "headCommit": head_commit,
[codex]         "headTag": head_tag,
[codex]         "manifestTag": manifest_tag,
[codex]         "matchesManifestTag": matches_manifest_tag,

[codex] phase7_sha256_file() {
[codex]     if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
[codex]         sha256sum "$1" | awk '{print $1}'
[codex]         return 0
[codex]     fi
[codex] 
[codex]     if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
[codex]         shasum -a 256 "$1" | awk '{print $1}'
[codex]         return 0
[codex]     fi
[codex] 
[codex]     echo "Neither sha256sum nor shasum is available" >&2
[codex]     return 1
[codex] }

[codex]         echo "Expected: $expected" >&2
[codex]         echo "Actual:   $actual" >&2
[codex]         return 1
[codex]     fi
[codex] }

[codex] # CI/CD Workflows
[codex] 
[codex] This document describes the GitHub Actions CI/CD setup for Budget Analyzer services and the orchestration repository.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Overview
[codex] 
[codex] All backend services use GitHub Actions for continuous integration. Each service has its own workflow that:
[codex] 
[codex] - Builds on every push to `main` and pull requests
[codex] - Runs all tests (unit, integration)
[codex] - Enforces code quality (Spotless formatting, Checkstyle)
[codex] - Uploads test results and build artifacts
[codex] 
[codex] ## Services with CI
[codex] 
[codex] | Service | Status Badge |
[codex] |---------|-------------|
[codex] | service-common | [![Build](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/service-common/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/service-common/actions/workflows/build.yml) |
[codex] | session-gateway | [![Build](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/session-gateway/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/session-gateway/actions/workflows/build.yml) |
[codex] | transaction-service | [![Build](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/transaction-service/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/transaction-service/actions/workflows/build.yml) |
[codex] | currency-service | [![Build](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/currency-service/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/currency-service/actions/workflows/build.yml) |
[codex] | permission-service | [![Build](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/permission-service/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/permission-service/actions/workflows/build.yml) |
[codex] | ext-authz | [![Build](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/ext-authz/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/ext-authz/actions/workflows/build.yml) |
[codex] 
[codex] ## Workflow Details
[codex] 
[codex] ### Triggers
[codex] 
[codex] All workflows trigger on:
[codex] 
[codex] - **Push to main**: Runs CI on every merge/commit
[codex] - **Pull requests**: Validates changes before merge
[codex] - **Manual dispatch**: Allows manual triggering via GitHub UI
[codex] 
[codex] ### Build Steps
[codex] 
[codex] 1. **Checkout**: Clone the repository
[codex] 2. **Setup JDK 25**: Install Temurin JDK 25
[codex] 3. **Setup Gradle**: Configure Gradle with caching
[codex] 4. **Resolve pinned `serviceCommon` version**: Read `gradle/libs.versions.toml`
[codex] 5. **Validate GitHub Packages access**: Fail fast if
[codex]    `SERVICE_COMMON_PACKAGES_USERNAME` /
[codex]    `SERVICE_COMMON_PACKAGES_READ_TOKEN` are missing or cannot read the pinned
[codex]    `service-core` / `service-web` POMs
[codex] 6. **Build with Gradle**: Run `./gradlew build` with
[codex]    `GITHUB_ACTOR` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` exported from those same secrets, which
[codex]    includes:
[codex]    - Compile Java source
[codex]    - Run Spotless formatting check
[codex]    - Run Checkstyle validation
[codex]    - Execute all tests
[codex]    - Package JAR
[codex] 7. **Upload artifacts**: Save test results and JARs
[codex] 
[codex] ### Code Quality
[codex] 
[codex] The build enforces code quality via:
[codex] 
[codex] - **Spotless**: Google Java Format (1.32.0)
[codex] - **Checkstyle**: Style rules from [checkstyle-config](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/checkstyle-config)
[codex] 
[codex] ### Dependencies
[codex] 
[codex] The Java service repos depend on `service-common`, but local development and
[codex] GitHub Actions intentionally use different resolution paths:
[codex] 
[codex] - local contributor builds stay `mavenLocal()`-first and rely on
[codex]   `publishToMavenLocal` plus orchestration/Tilt
[codex] - default GitHub Actions `build.yml` workflows resolve the pinned published
[codex]   `service-common` artifact version from GitHub Packages
[codex] - release workflows use the same GitHub Packages credential pair and the same
[codex]   remote artifact source
[codex] 
[codex] The checked-in `serviceCommon` entry in each consumer repo's
[codex] `gradle/libs.versions.toml` remains the source of truth for the version that CI
[codex] expects to exist remotely.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Release And Deployment Model
[codex] 
[codex] Budget Analyzer separates source tags, runtime artifact versions,
[codex] `service-common` Maven versions, image digests, and OCI deployment identity.
[codex] The production deployment truth is the checked-in, digest-pinned desired state
[codex] under `kubernetes/production/apps`, not a single global version string and not
[codex] live cluster status.
[codex] 
[codex] Terminology:
[codex] 
[codex] - Source tags are Git tags pushed to the deployable source repositories. A
[codex]   pushed `vX.Y.Z` source tag triggers the owning repository's release-image
[codex]   workflow.
[codex] - Docker tags are registry labels used to find and inspect images. For a
[codex]   `vX.Y.Z` source tag, the release-image workflows publish Docker label
[codex]   `X.Y.Z`.
[codex] - Image digests are the deployable artifact identity.
[codex] - The production manifest and image inventory are desired-state files. They do
[codex]   not record lifecycle status such as `accepted`, `pending`, or `deployed`.
[codex] - Live deployment status is observed from OCI by comparing running pods and
[codex]   runtime metadata with the checked-in desired state.
[codex] 
[codex] The normal OCI production flow has explicit local preparation steps, human
[codex] review, and one OCI-host apply command:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] # Local workstation
[codex] ./deploy/scripts/release/prepare-oci-manifest-from-current-stack.sh --source-tag vX.Y.Z --plan-only
[codex] ./deploy/scripts/release/prepare-oci-manifest-from-current-stack.sh --source-tag vX.Y.Z --push-tags
[codex] 
[codex] # After the owning GitHub Actions image workflows publish the expected GHCR tags
[codex] ./deploy/scripts/release/prepare-oci-manifest-from-current-stack.sh --source-tag vX.Y.Z --resolve-images
[codex] 
[codex] # OCI host, after the orchestration diff is reviewed, committed, pushed, and pulled
[codex] ./deploy/scripts/release/deploy-current-oci-manifest.sh
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] The recurring deploy script map and operator run order live in
[codex] [deploy/README.md](../deploy/README.md). This document owns the release and
[codex] deployment terminology.
[codex] 
[codex] The local preparation command validates the expected sibling repositories,
[codex] requires clean source workspaces, compares current artifact source state with
[codex] the checked-in production image inventory, previews source tag actions only for
[codex] changed artifacts, creates and pushes missing source tags when explicitly
[codex] requested, then stops so the operator can wait for the owning GitHub Actions
[codex] image workflows. Unchanged artifacts keep their existing digest-pinned images
[codex] and source metadata. Use `--lockstep` only for coordinated releases that should
[codex] force every managed artifact onto the requested source tag and Docker label.
[codex] The `--resolve-images` mode reads already-published GHCR tags for changed
[codex] artifacts, resolves immutable digests, updates the production manifest, image
[codex] inventory, app overlay, runtime metadata patch, and `/api-docs` release
[codex] metadata, then stops. Missing GHCR tags are a prerequisite failure in resolve
[codex] mode, not a polling loop. The local
[codex] preparation command does not build Docker images, push GHCR images directly,
[codex] deploy to OCI, require OCI kubeconfig access, or write lifecycle status.
[codex] GHCR image reads use the Docker Registry API bearer-token flow. Public packages
[codex] can resolve anonymously; private packages require `GHCR_USERNAME` and
[codex] `GHCR_TOKEN` with `read:packages` scope. GitHub SSH keys are not used by GHCR
[codex] image reads.
[codex] 
[codex] The final orchestration manifest commit necessarily happens after source tags
[codex] that build deployable images, including the `ext-authz` tag in the sibling
[codex] `budgetanalyzer/ext-authz` repo. Do not try to make the checked-in desired-state
[codex] manifest self-reference the commit that contains itself. Treat per-artifact
[codex] commit fields in the manifest as image build inputs; the orchestration revision
[codex] pulled by the OCI host is deploy evidence captured during apply.
[codex] 
[codex] The OCI deployment command applies the checked-in desired state from the
[codex] orchestration repo on the OCI host and verifies that live pods match it. The
[codex] old combined local-build/live-apply path is removed from the active deployment
[codex] surface.
[codex] 
[codex] `service-common` is a library release line, not the stack version. Release it
[codex] when `spring-platform`, `spring-cloud-platform`, `service-core`, or
[codex] `service-web` changes. Do not bump it only to ship a service image, route
[codex] change, documentation metadata fix, or production overlay update.
[codex] 
[codex] Tag helpers remain useful for human source management and rare named releases,
[codex] but tag names are not production correctness. OCI apply and verification use
[codex] the checked-in desired state and immutable image digests.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Orchestration Workflows
[codex] 
[codex] ### `security-guardrails.yml`
[codex] 
[codex] The orchestration repo now has a dedicated static security workflow for the
[codex] manifest guardrail suite. It is intentionally additive beside `test-setup.yml`;
[codex] it does not reuse the stale DinD suites as current security guardrails.
[codex] 
[codex] It now runs on every push to `main` and every pull request targeting `main`.
[codex] The narrower path filter was removed so guarded security surfaces cannot bypass
[codex] the workflow when a new file path is added to the static scope.
[codex] 
[codex] What it runs:
[codex] 
[codex] - `./scripts/guardrails/verify-static-security-manifests.sh`
[codex] - `./scripts/guardrails/verify-static-security-manifests.sh --self-test`
[codex] 
[codex] The workflow bootstraps repo-pinned `helm`, `kubectl`, `kubeconform`,
[codex] `kube-linter`, and `kyverno` binaries through
[codex] `scripts/bootstrap/install-verified-tool.sh`, then runs:
[codex] 
[codex] - schema validation for checked-in manifests, with explicit missing-schema
[codex]   allowances for checked-in CRD resources such as Istio, Gateway API, Kyverno,
[codex]   and Prometheus Operator `ServiceMonitor` objects
[codex] - rendered Kustomize schema validation for the production app and
[codex]   infrastructure overlays, so partial patch files stay excluded from
[codex]   standalone validation but are still checked after render; the schema-v2
[codex]   production deployment manifest is also excluded because it is desired-state
[codex]   metadata, not a Kubernetes resource
[codex] - repo-specific kube-linter checks with documented exceptions
[codex] - Kyverno CLI pass/fail fixtures
[codex] - a generated Kyverno replay for representative approved local Tilt
[codex]   `:tilt-&lt;hash>` deploy refs derived from the checked-in contract inventory
[codex] - a rendered Kyverno production-chart check that rejects mutable controller and
[codex]   hook image refs from `deploy/helm-values/kyverno.values.yaml`
[codex] - pattern scans for image pinning, namespace PSA labels, and lingering
[codex]   pipe-to-shell guidance in active setup docs/scripts
[codex] 
[codex] That directory split is intentional: CI-safe checks live under
[codex] `scripts/guardrails/`, shared installer/bootstrap helpers live under
[codex] `scripts/bootstrap/`, and the live-cluster proof remains in
[codex] `scripts/smoketest/` so GitHub Actions cannot silently drift into a
[codex] static-only substitute for the local runtime gate.
[codex] 
[codex] Use the same command locally to reproduce workflow failures without a cluster:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] ./scripts/guardrails/verify-static-security-manifests.sh
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] For full local security guardrail proof on a live cluster, use the separate
[codex] final gate:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] ./scripts/smoketest/verify-security-guardrails.sh
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] That wrapper intentionally stays out of GitHub Actions because the runtime
[codex] proof depends on a live local cluster. CI for the security guardrails remains
[codex] static-only.

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Configuration prepared; administrator activation is still required.
[codex] +
[codex] +This document owns the operating policy for dependency automation across the
[codex] +Budget Analyzer repositories. The preserved
[codex] +[September 6 dependency review](research/dependency-update-review-2026-09-06.md)
[codex] +is the historical acceptance benchmark; its observed versions are not bot
[codex] +targets. The executable rollout and acceptance sequence remains in the
[codex] +[dependency automation plan](plans/dependency-automation-plan.md).
[codex] +
[codex] +## Ownership and policy
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate is the only service allowed to open dependency update pull requests.
[codex] +Dependabot remains alert-only: keep the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts
[codex] +enabled, disable Dependabot version updates and overlapping Dependabot security
[codex] +update pull requests, and let Renovate consume alerts when its App permission
[codex] +allows that. Never enable automerge, including for security fixes.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared policy is
[codex] +[`renovate-presets/default.json`](../renovate-presets/default.json). Repository
[codex] +configuration extends it and adds only repository-specific manager paths and
[codex] +extraction rules. Routine pull requests are created weekly, with no more than
[codex] +three open routine pull requests and two new routine pull requests per hour in
[codex] +one repository. Vulnerability fixes use Renovate's dedicated alert path and an
[codex] +unrestricted schedule. Major, chart, stateful, platform, and checksum-coupled
[codex] +updates require Dependency Dashboard approval.
[codex] +
[codex] +Patch, minor, and major proposals remain distinct. Digest refreshes must retain
[codex] +an immutable digest and any image flavor suffix. Reviewers must independently
[codex] +verify Linux ARM64 support. An available tag or a changed digest is not evidence
[codex] +of architecture support, embedded package versions, vulnerability remediation,
[codex] +or upstream support status.
[codex] +
[codex] +The following stay outside Renovate ownership:
[codex] +
[codex] +- historical/generated outputs and the retained stale test suites
[codex] +- local `:latest` and generated `:tilt-*` images listed by the image-pinning
[codex] +  inventories
[codex] +- first-party production images and their synchronized manifest, inventory,
[codex] +  overlay, runtime metadata, and API-docs metadata
[codex] +- Pod Security compatibility labels
[codex] +- arbitrary per-platform checksum calculation
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate may propose checksum-coupled tool versions, but dashboard approval and
[codex] +the existing checksum verification remain mandatory. A reviewer must update the
[codex] +complete checksum table; no validation may be weakened to merge the proposal.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Cost and service boundary
[codex] +
[codex] +Use the open-source Renovate engine through the free Mend Renovate Community
[codex] +GitHub App. Do not provision a self-hosted bot or opt into paid Merge Confidence,
[codex] +enterprise scheduling, enhanced cache, a trial, or another subscription. The
[codex] +selected security evidence uses GitHub's dependency graph and Dependabot alerts,
[codex] +Gradle's open-source basic dependency-submission path, Trivy, `npm audit`, and
[codex] +`govulncheck`.
[codex] +
[codex] +GitHub Actions usage is separate from Mend hosting. Public repositories can use
[codex] +standard hosted Linux runners. Before enabling automation for a private
[codex] +repository, confirm its included Actions allowance and that paid overages are
[codex] +disabled. Stop for user direction if required coverage needs spending or a
[codex] +capability unavailable on the free offering.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Activation procedure
[codex] +
[codex] +Configuration preparation does not authorize GitHub setting changes. A
[codex] +repository administrator performs activation only after all rollout phases have
[codex] +prepared and validated their files:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Publish the orchestration repository and its shared preset before publishing
[codex] +   consumer configurations.
[codex] +2. Confirm repository visibility, Actions billing/overage settings, and that the
[codex] +   free Mend service supports every scoped repository and required authenticated
[codex] +   Maven lookup within its job limits.
[codex] +3. Install the Renovate Community App only on the repositories listed in the
[codex] +   rollout plan. Grant read access to Dependabot alerts when available.
[codex] +4. Enable the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts. Disable Dependabot version
[codex] +   updates and automatic Dependabot security-update pull requests.
[codex] +5. Configure private Maven access only through Mend-supported encrypted secrets
[codex] +   and host rules. Never commit a token and never use `pull_request_target` to
[codex] +   expose trusted credentials to dependency branches.
[codex] +6. Run onboarding for orchestration first. Inspect the resolved configuration,
[codex] +   extraction logs, dashboard, job duration, and any rate-limit or timeout
[codex] +   message before enabling consumers.
[codex] +7. Record every baseline item in the coverage report as reproduced, superseded,
[codex] +   false positive with evidence, or missing. Update discovery, advisory evidence,
[codex] +   and lifecycle assessment are separate results.
[codex] +
[codex] +The Community service's documented single concurrent organization job,
[codex] +approximately four-hour scheduling, and 30-minute timeout are acceptable only if
[codex] +the pilot completes in practice. A timeout or unsupported authenticated lookup
[codex] +blocks broader activation; it is not a reason to omit dependencies.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Local validation and dry run
[codex] +
[codex] +The focused workflow validates both JSON files with Renovate's official
[codex] +`renovate-config-validator` under Node 24. Before publishing the preset, run the
[codex] +same strict schema validation locally. For an unpublished-preset dry run, load
[codex] +`renovate-presets/default.json` as the local self-hosted configuration, suppress
[codex] +repository config discovery, and process the checkout with the local platform.
[codex] +Use debug logging and `--dry-run=full`; do not provide a GitHub token or enable a
[codex] +write-capable platform mode.
[codex] +
[codex] +Extraction and lookup evidence belongs in
[codex] +[`docs/research/dependency-automation-coverage.md`](research/dependency-automation-coverage.md),
[codex] +not in a second desired-version inventory.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Failure triage
[codex] +
[codex] +- **Configuration error:** reproduce with the pinned validator version. Treat
[codex] +  warnings and migrations as failures; correct the preset or repository config.
[codex] +- **No extraction:** check the owning file's native manager pattern or adjacent
[codex] +  annotation and compare debug logs. Do not seed the historical expected version
[codex] +  into configuration.
[codex] +- **No lookup or wrong package:** verify the real datasource identity, chart
[codex] +  name, registry URL, tag prefix, build suffix, and flavor suffix. Record an
[codex] +  unresolved standard-tool gap instead of adding a custom crawler.
[codex] +- **Authentication or resolution failure:** preserve the failure. Fix encrypted
[codex] +  Maven/registry access in the supported trust boundary; do not use Maven Local,
[codex] +  drop internal dependencies, or swallow the error.
[codex] +- **Finding without an update:** retain the Dependabot/scanner finding and route
[codex] +  inherited or transitive remediation to the owning service. An update pull
[codex] +  request is not proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] +- **CI failure on a bot branch:** determine whether the proposal needs its
[codex] +  documented checksum, chart rendering, ARM64, state migration, or cross-repo
[codex] +  companion review. Do not relax a guardrail or create orchestration drift.
[codex] +- **Scanner database/download failure:** report the job as failed separately
[codex] +  from vulnerability findings. Never turn an unavailable scan into a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate discovery and vulnerability scanners do not comprehensively establish
[codex] +end-of-life status. Owners must still perform a quarterly support-policy review
[codex] +against upstream lifecycle sources.

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Configuration prepared; administrator activation is still required.
[codex] +
[codex] +This document owns the operating policy for dependency automation across the
[codex] +Budget Analyzer repositories. The preserved
[codex] +[September 6 dependency review](research/dependency-update-review-2026-09-06.md)
[codex] +is the historical acceptance benchmark; its observed versions are not bot
[codex] +targets. The executable rollout and acceptance sequence remains in the
[codex] +[dependency automation plan](plans/dependency-automation-plan.md).
[codex] +
[codex] +## Ownership and policy
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate is the only service allowed to open dependency update pull requests.
[codex] +Dependabot remains alert-only: keep the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts
[codex] +enabled, disable Dependabot version updates and overlapping Dependabot security
[codex] +update pull requests, and let Renovate consume alerts when its App permission
[codex] +allows that. Never enable automerge, including for security fixes.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared policy is
[codex] +[`renovate-presets/default.json`](../renovate-presets/default.json). Repository
[codex] +configuration extends it and adds only repository-specific manager paths and
[codex] +extraction rules. Routine pull requests are created weekly, with no more than
[codex] +three open routine pull requests and two new routine pull requests per hour in
[codex] +one repository. Vulnerability fixes use Renovate's dedicated alert path and an
[codex] +unrestricted schedule. Major, chart, stateful, platform, and checksum-coupled
[codex] +updates require Dependency Dashboard approval.
[codex] +
[codex] +Patch, minor, and major proposals remain distinct. Digest refreshes must retain
[codex] +an immutable digest and any image flavor suffix. Reviewers must independently
[codex] +verify Linux ARM64 support. An available tag or a changed digest is not evidence
[codex] +of architecture support, embedded package versions, vulnerability remediation,
[codex] +or upstream support status.
[codex] +
[codex] +The following stay outside Renovate ownership:
[codex] +
[codex] +- historical/generated outputs and the retained stale test suites
[codex] +- local `:latest` and generated `:tilt-*` images listed by the image-pinning
[codex] +  inventories
[codex] +- first-party production images and their synchronized manifest, inventory,
[codex] +  overlay, runtime metadata, and API-docs metadata
[codex] +- Pod Security compatibility labels
[codex] +- arbitrary per-platform checksum calculation
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate may propose checksum-coupled tool versions, but dashboard approval and
[codex] +the existing checksum verification remain mandatory. A reviewer must update the
[codex] +complete checksum table; no validation may be weakened to merge the proposal.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Cost and service boundary
[codex] +
[codex] +Use the open-source Renovate engine through the free Mend Renovate Community
[codex] +GitHub App. Do not provision a self-hosted bot or opt into paid Merge Confidence,
[codex] +enterprise scheduling, enhanced cache, a trial, or another subscription. The
[codex] +selected security evidence uses GitHub's dependency graph and Dependabot alerts,
[codex] +Gradle's open-source basic dependency-submission path, Trivy, `npm audit`, and
[codex] +`govulncheck`.
[codex] +
[codex] +GitHub Actions usage is separate from Mend hosting. Public repositories can use
[codex] +standard hosted Linux runners. Before enabling automation for a private
[codex] +repository, confirm its included Actions allowance and that paid overages are
[codex] +disabled. Stop for user direction if required coverage needs spending or a
[codex] +capability unavailable on the free offering.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Activation procedure
[codex] +
[codex] +Configuration preparation does not authorize GitHub setting changes. A
[codex] +repository administrator performs activation only after all rollout phases have
[codex] +prepared and validated their files:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Publish the orchestration repository and its shared preset before publishing
[codex] +   consumer configurations.
[codex] +2. Confirm repository visibility, Actions billing/overage settings, and that the
[codex] +   free Mend service supports every scoped repository and required authenticated
[codex] +   Maven lookup within its job limits.
[codex] +3. Install the Renovate Community App only on the repositories listed in the
[codex] +   rollout plan. Grant read access to Dependabot alerts when available.
[codex] +4. Enable the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts. Disable Dependabot version
[codex] +   updates and automatic Dependabot security-update pull requests.
[codex] +5. Configure private Maven access only through Mend-supported encrypted secrets
[codex] +   and host rules. Never commit a token and never use `pull_request_target` to
[codex] +   expose trusted credentials to dependency branches.
[codex] +6. Run onboarding for orchestration first. Inspect the resolved configuration,
[codex] +   extraction logs, dashboard, job duration, and any rate-limit or timeout
[codex] +   message before enabling consumers.
[codex] +7. Record every baseline item in the coverage report as reproduced, superseded,
[codex] +   false positive with evidence, or missing. Update discovery, advisory evidence,
[codex] +   and lifecycle assessment are separate results.
[codex] +
[codex] +The Community service's documented single concurrent organization job,
[codex] +approximately four-hour scheduling, and 30-minute timeout are acceptable only if
[codex] +the pilot completes in practice. A timeout or unsupported authenticated lookup
[codex] +blocks broader activation; it is not a reason to omit dependencies.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Local validation and dry run
[codex] +
[codex] +The focused workflow validates both JSON files with Renovate's official
[codex] +`renovate-config-validator` under Node 24. Before publishing the preset, run the
[codex] +same strict schema validation locally. For an unpublished-preset dry run, load
[codex] +`renovate-presets/default.json` as the local self-hosted configuration, suppress
[codex] +repository config discovery, and process the checkout with the local platform.
[codex] +Use debug logging and `--dry-run=full`; do not provide a GitHub token or enable a
[codex] +write-capable platform mode.
[codex] +
[codex] +Extraction and lookup evidence belongs in
[codex] +[`docs/research/dependency-automation-coverage.md`](research/dependency-automation-coverage.md),
[codex] +not in a second desired-version inventory.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Failure triage
[codex] +
[codex] +- **Configuration error:** reproduce with the pinned validator version. Treat
[codex] +  warnings and migrations as failures; correct the preset or repository config.
[codex] +- **No extraction:** check the owning file's native manager pattern or adjacent
[codex] +  annotation and compare debug logs. Do not seed the historical expected version
[codex] +  into configuration.
[codex] +- **No lookup or wrong package:** verify the real datasource identity, chart
[codex] +  name, registry URL, tag prefix, build suffix, and flavor suffix. Record an
[codex] +  unresolved standard-tool gap instead of adding a custom crawler.
[codex] +- **Authentication or resolution failure:** preserve the failure. Fix encrypted
[codex] +  Maven/registry access in the supported trust boundary; do not use Maven Local,
[codex] +  drop internal dependencies, or swallow the error.
[codex] +- **Finding without an update:** retain the Dependabot/scanner finding and route
[codex] +  inherited or transitive remediation to the owning service. An update pull
[codex] +  request is not proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] +- **CI failure on a bot branch:** determine whether the proposal needs its
[codex] +  documented checksum, chart rendering, ARM64, state migration, or cross-repo
[codex] +  companion review. Do not relax a guardrail or create orchestration drift.
[codex] +- **Scanner database/download failure:** report the job as failed separately
[codex] +  from vulnerability findings. Never turn an unavailable scan into a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate discovery and vulnerability scanners do not comprehensively establish
[codex] +end-of-life status. Owners must still perform a quarterly support-policy review
[codex] +against upstream lifecycle sources.

[codex] +
[codex] +This document owns the operating policy for dependency automation across the
[codex] +Budget Analyzer repositories. The preserved
[codex] +[September 6 dependency review](research/dependency-update-review-2026-09-06.md)
[codex] +is the historical acceptance benchmark; its observed versions are not bot
[codex] +targets. The executable rollout and acceptance sequence remains in the
[codex] +[dependency automation plan](plans/dependency-automation-plan.md).
[codex] +
[codex] +## Ownership and policy
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate is the only service allowed to open dependency update pull requests.
[codex] +Dependabot remains alert-only: keep the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts
[codex] +enabled, disable Dependabot version updates and overlapping Dependabot security
[codex] +update pull requests, and let Renovate consume alerts when its App permission
[codex] +allows that. Never enable automerge, including for security fixes.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared policy is
[codex] +[`renovate-presets/default.json`](../renovate-presets/default.json). Repository
[codex] +configuration extends it and adds only repository-specific manager paths and
[codex] +extraction rules. Routine pull requests are created weekly, with no more than
[codex] +three open routine pull requests and two new routine pull requests per hour in
[codex] +one repository. Vulnerability fixes use Renovate's dedicated alert path and an
[codex] +unrestricted schedule. Major, chart, stateful, platform, and checksum-coupled
[codex] +updates require Dependency Dashboard approval.
[codex] +
[codex] +Patch, minor, and major proposals remain distinct. Digest refreshes must retain
[codex] +an immutable digest and any image flavor suffix. Reviewers must independently
[codex] +verify Linux ARM64 support. An available tag or a changed digest is not evidence
[codex] +of architecture support, embedded package versions, vulnerability remediation,
[codex] +or upstream support status.
[codex] +
[codex] +The following stay outside Renovate ownership:
[codex] +
[codex] +- historical/generated outputs and the retained stale test suites
[codex] +- local `:latest` and generated `:tilt-*` images listed by the image-pinning
[codex] +  inventories
[codex] +- first-party production images and their synchronized manifest, inventory,
[codex] +  overlay, runtime metadata, and API-docs metadata
[codex] +- Pod Security compatibility labels
[codex] +- arbitrary per-platform checksum calculation
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate may propose checksum-coupled tool versions, but dashboard approval and
[codex] +the existing checksum verification remain mandatory. A reviewer must update the
[codex] +complete checksum table; no validation may be weakened to merge the proposal.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Cost and service boundary
[codex] +
[codex] +Use the open-source Renovate engine through the free Mend Renovate Community
[codex] +GitHub App. Do not provision a self-hosted bot or opt into paid Merge Confidence,
[codex] +enterprise scheduling, enhanced cache, a trial, or another subscription. The
[codex] +selected security evidence uses GitHub's dependency graph and Dependabot alerts,
[codex] +Gradle's open-source basic dependency-submission path, Trivy, `npm audit`, and
[codex] +`govulncheck`.
[codex] +
[codex] +GitHub Actions usage is separate from Mend hosting. Public repositories can use
[codex] +standard hosted Linux runners. Before enabling automation for a private
[codex] +repository, confirm its included Actions allowance and that paid overages are
[codex] +disabled. Stop for user direction if required coverage needs spending or a
[codex] +capability unavailable on the free offering.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Activation procedure
[codex] +
[codex] +Configuration preparation does not authorize GitHub setting changes. A
[codex] +repository administrator performs activation only after all rollout phases have
[codex] +prepared and validated their files:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Publish the orchestration repository and its shared preset before publishing
[codex] +   consumer configurations.
[codex] +2. Confirm repository visibility, Actions billing/overage settings, and that the
[codex] +   free Mend service supports every scoped repository and required authenticated
[codex] +   Maven lookup within its job limits.
[codex] +3. Install the Renovate Community App only on the repositories listed in the
[codex] +   rollout plan. Grant read access to Dependabot alerts when available.
[codex] +4. Enable the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts. Disable Dependabot version
[codex] +   updates and automatic Dependabot security-update pull requests.
[codex] +5. Configure private Maven access only through Mend-supported encrypted secrets
[codex] +   and host rules. Never commit a token and never use `pull_request_target` to
[codex] +   expose trusted credentials to dependency branches.
[codex] +6. Run onboarding for orchestration first. Inspect the resolved configuration,
[codex] +   extraction logs, dashboard, job duration, and any rate-limit or timeout
[codex] +   message before enabling consumers.
[codex] +7. Record every baseline item in the coverage report as reproduced, superseded,
[codex] +   false positive with evidence, or missing. Update discovery, advisory evidence,
[codex] +   and lifecycle assessment are separate results.
[codex] +
[codex] +The Community service's documented single concurrent organization job,
[codex] +approximately four-hour scheduling, and 30-minute timeout are acceptable only if
[codex] +the pilot completes in practice. A timeout or unsupported authenticated lookup
[codex] +blocks broader activation; it is not a reason to omit dependencies.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Local validation and dry run
[codex] +
[codex] +The focused workflow validates both JSON files with Renovate's official
[codex] +`renovate-config-validator` under Node 24. Before publishing the preset, run the
[codex] +same strict schema validation locally. For an unpublished-preset dry run, load
[codex] +`renovate-presets/default.json` as the local self-hosted configuration, suppress
[codex] +repository config discovery, and process the checkout with the local platform.
[codex] +Use debug logging and `--dry-run=full`; do not provide a GitHub token or enable a
[codex] +write-capable platform mode.
[codex] +
[codex] +Extraction and lookup evidence belongs in
[codex] +[`docs/research/dependency-automation-coverage.md`](research/dependency-automation-coverage.md),
[codex] +not in a second desired-version inventory.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Failure triage
[codex] +
[codex] +- **Configuration error:** reproduce with the pinned validator version. Treat
[codex] +  warnings and migrations as failures; correct the preset or repository config.
[codex] +- **No extraction:** check the owning file's native manager pattern or adjacent
[codex] +  annotation and compare debug logs. Do not seed the historical expected version
[codex] +  into configuration.
[codex] +- **No lookup or wrong package:** verify the real datasource identity, chart
[codex] +  name, registry URL, tag prefix, build suffix, and flavor suffix. Record an
[codex] +  unresolved standard-tool gap instead of adding a custom crawler.
[codex] +- **Authentication or resolution failure:** preserve the failure. Fix encrypted
[codex] +  Maven/registry access in the supported trust boundary; do not use Maven Local,
[codex] +  drop internal dependencies, or swallow the error.
[codex] +- **Finding without an update:** retain the Dependabot/scanner finding and route
[codex] +  inherited or transitive remediation to the owning service. An update pull
[codex] +  request is not proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] +- **CI failure on a bot branch:** determine whether the proposal needs its
[codex] +  documented checksum, chart rendering, ARM64, state migration, or cross-repo
[codex] +  companion review. Do not relax a guardrail or create orchestration drift.
[codex] +- **Scanner database/download failure:** report the job as failed separately
[codex] +  from vulnerability findings. Never turn an unavailable scan into a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate discovery and vulnerability scanners do not comprehensively establish
[codex] +end-of-life status. Owners must still perform a quarterly support-policy review
[codex] +against upstream lifecycle sources.

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Configuration prepared; administrator activation is still required.
[codex] +
[codex] +This document owns the operating policy for dependency automation across the
[codex] +Budget Analyzer repositories. The preserved
[codex] +[September 6 dependency review](research/dependency-update-review-2026-09-06.md)
[codex] +is the historical acceptance benchmark; its observed versions are not bot
[codex] +targets. The executable rollout and acceptance sequence remains in the
[codex] +[dependency automation plan](plans/dependency-automation-plan.md).
[codex] +
[codex] +## Ownership and policy
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate is the only service allowed to open dependency update pull requests.
[codex] +Dependabot remains alert-only: keep the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts
[codex] +enabled, disable Dependabot version updates and overlapping Dependabot security
[codex] +update pull requests, and let Renovate consume alerts when its App permission
[codex] +allows that. Never enable automerge, including for security fixes.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared policy is
[codex] +[`renovate-presets/default.json`](../renovate-presets/default.json). Repository
[codex] +configuration extends it and adds only repository-specific manager paths and
[codex] +extraction rules. Routine pull requests are created weekly, with no more than
[codex] +three open routine pull requests and two new routine pull requests per hour in
[codex] +one repository. Vulnerability fixes use Renovate's dedicated alert path and an
[codex] +unrestricted schedule. Major, chart, stateful, platform, and checksum-coupled
[codex] +updates require Dependency Dashboard approval.
[codex] +
[codex] +Patch, minor, and major proposals remain distinct. Digest refreshes must retain
[codex] +an immutable digest and any image flavor suffix. Reviewers must independently
[codex] +verify Linux ARM64 support. An available tag or a changed digest is not evidence
[codex] +of architecture support, embedded package versions, vulnerability remediation,
[codex] +or upstream support status.
[codex] +
[codex] +The following stay outside Renovate ownership:
[codex] +
[codex] +- historical/generated outputs and the retained stale test suites
[codex] +- local `:latest` and generated `:tilt-*` images listed by the image-pinning
[codex] +  inventories
[codex] +- first-party production images and their synchronized manifest, inventory,
[codex] +  overlay, runtime metadata, and API-docs metadata
[codex] +- Pod Security compatibility labels
[codex] +- arbitrary per-platform checksum calculation
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate may propose checksum-coupled tool versions, but dashboard approval and
[codex] +the existing checksum verification remain mandatory. A reviewer must update the
[codex] +complete checksum table; no validation may be weakened to merge the proposal.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Cost and service boundary
[codex] +
[codex] +Use the open-source Renovate engine through the free Mend Renovate Community
[codex] +GitHub App. Do not provision a self-hosted bot or opt into paid Merge Confidence,
[codex] +enterprise scheduling, enhanced cache, a trial, or another subscription. The
[codex] +selected security evidence uses GitHub's dependency graph and Dependabot alerts,
[codex] +Gradle's open-source basic dependency-submission path, Trivy, `npm audit`, and
[codex] +`govulncheck`.
[codex] +
[codex] +GitHub Actions usage is separate from Mend hosting. Public repositories can use
[codex] +standard hosted Linux runners. Before enabling automation for a private
[codex] +repository, confirm its included Actions allowance and that paid overages are
[codex] +disabled. Stop for user direction if required coverage needs spending or a
[codex] +capability unavailable on the free offering.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Activation procedure
[codex] +
[codex] +Configuration preparation does not authorize GitHub setting changes. A
[codex] +repository administrator performs activation only after all rollout phases have
[codex] +prepared and validated their files:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Publish the orchestration repository and its shared preset before publishing
[codex] +   consumer configurations.
[codex] +2. Confirm repository visibility, Actions billing/overage settings, and that the
[codex] +   free Mend service supports every scoped repository and required authenticated
[codex] +   Maven lookup within its job limits.
[codex] +3. Install the Renovate Community App only on the repositories listed in the
[codex] +   rollout plan. Grant read access to Dependabot alerts when available.
[codex] +4. Enable the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts. Disable Dependabot version
[codex] +   updates and automatic Dependabot security-update pull requests.
[codex] +5. Configure private Maven access only through Mend-supported encrypted secrets
[codex] +   and host rules. Never commit a token and never use `pull_request_target` to
[codex] +   expose trusted credentials to dependency branches.
[codex] +6. Run onboarding for orchestration first. Inspect the resolved configuration,
[codex] +   extraction logs, dashboard, job duration, and any rate-limit or timeout
[codex] +   message before enabling consumers.
[codex] +7. Record every baseline item in the coverage report as reproduced, superseded,
[codex] +   false positive with evidence, or missing. Update discovery, advisory evidence,
[codex] +   and lifecycle assessment are separate results.
[codex] +
[codex] +The Community service's documented single concurrent organization job,
[codex] +approximately four-hour scheduling, and 30-minute timeout are acceptable only if
[codex] +the pilot completes in practice. A timeout or unsupported authenticated lookup
[codex] +blocks broader activation; it is not a reason to omit dependencies.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Local validation and dry run
[codex] +
[codex] +The focused workflow validates both JSON files with Renovate's official
[codex] +`renovate-config-validator` under Node 24. Before publishing the preset, run the
[codex] +same strict schema validation locally. For an unpublished-preset dry run, load
[codex] +`renovate-presets/default.json` as the local self-hosted configuration, suppress
[codex] +repository config discovery, and process the checkout with the local platform.
[codex] +Use debug logging and `--dry-run=full`; do not provide a GitHub token or enable a
[codex] +write-capable platform mode.
[codex] +
[codex] +Extraction and lookup evidence belongs in
[codex] +[`docs/research/dependency-automation-coverage.md`](research/dependency-automation-coverage.md),
[codex] +not in a second desired-version inventory.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Failure triage
[codex] +
[codex] +- **Configuration error:** reproduce with the pinned validator version. Treat
[codex] +  warnings and migrations as failures; correct the preset or repository config.
[codex] +- **No extraction:** check the owning file's native manager pattern or adjacent
[codex] +  annotation and compare debug logs. Do not seed the historical expected version
[codex] +  into configuration.
[codex] +- **No lookup or wrong package:** verify the real datasource identity, chart
[codex] +  name, registry URL, tag prefix, build suffix, and flavor suffix. Record an
[codex] +  unresolved standard-tool gap instead of adding a custom crawler.
[codex] +- **Authentication or resolution failure:** preserve the failure. Fix encrypted
[codex] +  Maven/registry access in the supported trust boundary; do not use Maven Local,
[codex] +  drop internal dependencies, or swallow the error.
[codex] +- **Finding without an update:** retain the Dependabot/scanner finding and route
[codex] +  inherited or transitive remediation to the owning service. An update pull
[codex] +  request is not proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] +- **CI failure on a bot branch:** determine whether the proposal needs its
[codex] +  documented checksum, chart rendering, ARM64, state migration, or cross-repo
[codex] +  companion review. Do not relax a guardrail or create orchestration drift.
[codex] +- **Scanner database/download failure:** report the job as failed separately
[codex] +  from vulnerability findings. Never turn an unavailable scan into a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate discovery and vulnerability scanners do not comprehensively establish
[codex] +end-of-life status. Owners must still perform a quarterly support-policy review
[codex] +against upstream lifecycle sources.
